title: Restart Intensity Blizzards (intensity/period) & Upward Crash Escalation
solutionExplanation: Implements the sliding-window crash intensity rate limiter algorithm and calculates downstream reverse-order termination and forward-order restart plans for rest_for_one pipelines.

otpDocCards.signature: sup_flags() = #{strategy => strategy(), intensity => non_neg_integer(), period => pos_integer()}
otpDocCards.description: Defines restart frequency threshold (intensity / period). If exceeded, supervisor terminates itself with shutdown to escalate upward.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Maintained as an O(N) timestamp queue inside the supervisor loop.

mentalModelCheck.question: When a supervisor exceeds its MaxR restarts within MaxT seconds, why does it shut itself down instead of just giving up on that single worker?

options.label: To escalate the failure up the supervision tree, allowing a higher-level supervisor with a broader architectural perspective to restart the entire subsystem.
options.explanation: Supervisors isolate failures locally until their restart budget is exhausted. When exceeded, escalating to the parent supervisor prevents infinite localized loops.

options.label: Because the supervisor process runs out of memory from storing crash timestamps.
options.explanation: The timestamp queue is tiny (pruned to MaxT seconds); shutdown is a deliberate architectural escalation mechanism.

options.label: Because the BEAM VM automatically sends a kill signal to any supervisor whose worker crashes.
options.explanation: The BEAM VM never kills supervisors automatically; the supervisor decides to terminate itself via its sup_flags contract.

options.label: To reboot the host operating system.
options.explanation: Erlang supervision trees operate purely within the user-space BEAM runtime.
